aspects.says: continue in a while loop goes straight back to the condition, so an update written after it is skipped and the loop can spin on one element forever.
basis: section:continue in a while Loop Jumps to the Condition, Past the Update at the Bottom

aspects.says: The condition of a do-while can't see a variable declared in its body, so what it tests is declared before do.
basis: section:A do-while Fits a Loop Whose First Pass Produces What the Condition Tests
aspects.reason: the compiler enforces it: no wrong solution compiles, so no test can grade it

aspects.says: A do-while makes its first pass before the test, so it fits a loop whose condition reads what a pass produces, such as a page cursor; a while loop there may never run.
basis: section:A do-while Fits a Loop Whose First Pass Produces What the Condition Tests

aspects.says: A do-while over input that may be empty runs its body once on nothing.
basis: section:A do-while Fits a Loop Whose First Pass Produces What the Condition Tests

aspects.says: A loop ends only if its exit exists for every input: a counter tested with <= against the largest value of its type wraps and never fails the test.
basis: section:A Loop Ends Only If Its Condition Can Become False for Every Input

aspects.says: A floating-point loop tested with != can step past its target and never end; test it with < or >.
basis: section:A Loop Ends Only If Its Condition Can Become False for Every Input
aspects.reason: floating-point representation belongs to unit 1.1.1, whose practices grade it; here it is one sentence that applies the same exit check

aspects.says: A binary search's invariant decides its condition, its updates and which way its midpoint rounds; the midpoint is computed so that it can't overflow.
basis: section:The Invariant Decides the Condition, the Updates and the Midpoint
section:Spot the Problem: Two Conventions in One Loop

aspects.says: Taking <= from the closed-interval convention and high = mid from the other makes the search probe the last candidate forever.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: Two Conventions in One Loop

aspects.says: A loop condition that another thread makes false needs the visibility and waiting rules of units 6.2.2 and 6.2.1.
basis: section:A Loop Ends Only If Its Condition Can Become False for Every Input
aspects.reason: a pointer to units 6.2.1 and 6.2.2, whose practices grade it
